DDInter1845.mechanism: Monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) may potentiate the hypotensive effect of some medications. MAOIs alone quite commonly produce orthostatic hypotension. This effect may stem from a gradual MAOI-induced accumulation of false neurotransmitters in peripheral adrenergic neurons that have minimal activity at alpha- and beta-adrenergic receptors, resulting in a functional block of sympathetic neurotransmission. The interaction has been reported with the concomitant use of beta-blockers.
